statement: automated evidence across authentication and session handling, request-forgery and content-policy and upload and traversal and server-side-request boundaries, query and identifier and pagination and exhaustion inputs, row and field and action and report and export and event and log non-disclosure, maker-checker and separation of duty and step-up and human proof and confused-deputy cases, idempotency conflict and operation ownership, extension signature and trust rotation and revocation and generation fencing, ambient authority and out-of-process controls, secret sources and rotation and redaction across every channel, audit tamper evidence and archival, and tenant isolation under concurrency and noisy-neighbour load.
note: Each sub-area names the application tests that prove it and the CI job that runs each one. Scanners in the security workflow supplement these application authorization tests; they never substitute for them. A sub-area without evidence must carry a reasoned out_of_scope entry naming its owning finding. tests/Architecture/SecurityQualificationMatrixTest.php enforces both rules and that every referenced test exists and is run by its job.

jobs..github/workflows/ci.yml#quality: PHP 8.5 quality: the unit and architecture suites.
jobs..github/workflows/ci.yml#database: PHP 8.5 on MariaDB, MySQL and PostgreSQL: the complete suite, including integration and functional tests.
jobs..github/workflows/security.yml#source-an: Security: the named P7-C Studio preview invocation, dependency audit, secret scanning and image scans.

evidence.proves: A wrong administrator credential creates no session and is answered on the form.
Unknown accounts, wrong passwords and unavailable memberships are indistinguishable on the portal.
The Redis-backed sign-in throttle window opens, closes and clears against the real store.
The eleventh attempt inside a window is refused.
No password is silently truncated before hashing.

sub_areas.title: Session cookie attributes and middleware coverage

evidence.proves: The live pipeline issues the exact HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, path-scoped and Secure-when-TLS administrator cookies.
The same exact attribute set holds for the portal session and its sign-in token.
An administrator cookie never authenticates the portal surface.

sub_areas.title: Idle and absolute expiry, rotation and browser binding

evidence.proves: Idle and absolute expiry are enforced by the stored sessions of both browser surfaces.
Idle expiry is judged at the exact instant.
Privilege change rotates the session and retires the previous cookie.
A stolen cookie replayed from another browser is refused before identity load.

sub_areas.title: Credential change and grant revocation end live sessions and tokens

evidence.proves: Removing a grant invalidates an issued bearer token on the next verification.
A password change proves the current password and retires every session.
Emergency token revocation also ends the subject browser sessions.
A session minted under a superseded security epoch no longer resolves.
Over REST, a user manager cannot reset the password or second factor of an account stronger than itself.
Authority held only through an organization membership, even an inactive one, bounds a credential takeover.
Break-glass console recovery is pinned at the ceiling for grant-holding accounts, pending a maintainer decision.
The access screen's stepped-up context still reaches every audited recovery act: password reset, second-factor retirement and session termination.

sub_areas.title: Bearer token audience, purpose, site and header binding

evidence.proves: Every authenticated machine request names exactly one site.
An ambiguous Authorization header is refused before verification.
Tokens are bound to an audience and purpose pair.
Every token lookup is bound to the adapter and the site.
Cookies, query-string tokens and foreign or repeated site headers confer no machine authority over HTTP.
An ordinary user can change only their own password.
Guessing the current password through self-service is throttled.
The administrative reset cannot replace the actor own password without proof.

areas.title: Request-forgery, content-policy, upload, traversal and server-side-request boundaries

sub_areas.title: Cross-site request forgery, including login forgery

evidence.proves: A forged or missing sign-in token never authenticates.
A forged portal sign-in token is refused before authentication and rotated.
A token from another session is refused.
A wrong header token is not rescued by a correct field.
The portal token is bound to its own session.

sub_areas.title: Content security policy and response hardening headers

evidence.proves: Every response carries the hardened header set and a per-response nonce.
No response admits an inline style source.
The live administrator and portal responses carry the no-inline-style policy.
Served SVG media is sandboxed by its own policy.
Only exact admissible script origins can widen the script directive.
Administered wording, now also writable over REST, cannot carry active markup into trusted rendering.
Substituted values are escaped even inside trusted catalogue markup.

sub_areas.title: Upload content-type confusion and executable payloads

evidence.proves: Executable or unknown uploads are refused by byte detection.
SVG is never accepted from an upload.
A Studio binary upload grant is bound to the fresh administrator session.
An imported body whose declared type disagrees with its bytes is refused and deleted.
Over HTTP, script, markup, SVG and mislabelled uploads are refused by their bytes and a polyglot is stored and served inertly under its detected type.
The REST raw-body upload judges bytes and keeps only the base name of a traversal-shaped filename.
A symbolic link in a deployed extension is refused.
Export storage refuses direct object keys.
Console document inputs refuse symbolic links.
The trusted runtime loads only from a resolved non-link root.
Every URL-to-file route refuses encoded and literal traversal like a missing file, and a traversal-shaped delete removes nothing.
Parent, absolute, backslash, nested and symbolic-link archive entries refuse the whole extension package.

sub_areas.title: Server-side request forgery through outbound fetchers, including redirect rebinding

evidence.proves: A DNS answer set mixing public and private addresses is refused before connecting.
A host that rebinds to a refused address between checks is refused.
Every redirect hop repeats lexical, DNS and pinning checks.
Only globally routable addresses are admitted.
A redirect is revalidated as a fresh candidate.
The revocation feed refuses plaintext origins.
No internal-address spelling or loopback-resolving name reaches a real loopback listener through the production importer.
The revocation feed transport refuses every non-TLS scheme before connecting.

areas.title: Query, identifier, pagination and exhaustion inputs

sub_areas.title: Closed query grammar with no injection path

evidence.proves: Every surface builds queries from one closed, bounded grammar.
Unknown query members are refused rather than ignored.
A filter tree is refused before it exceeds its node budget.
Browser filters and searches are bounded.
Malformed and missing export identifiers are indistinguishable.
Foreign identifiers stay unavailable.
Denied and missing Studio reads collapse to one answer.
The MCP operation status tool cannot enumerate operations.
Over HTTP, missing, malformed and forbidden identifiers get the same answer.
Record cursors are signed and tampering is refused.
A tampered Studio resource cursor is refused.
Deep offsets are refused before any statement runs.
A page beyond the practical bound is refused.
Page limits are filled after authorization filtering, so paging cannot reveal withheld rows.
History paging refuses ambiguous identities at every cursor position.
Machine limits are enforced by name, and overflowing browser pages fall back instead of failing.
A media page at the integer limit is an empty page, not an overflow.
A declared oversized body is refused.
An undeclared oversized body is refused while streaming.
History, value and export bounds are enforced.
A synchronous report that exceeds its row limit is refused with guidance.
An oversized extension archive is refused before it is copied.
Studio recovery writes are rate limited.
Over HTTP, oversized bodies, nesting bombs and unusable keys are refused with client errors.

areas.title: Row, field, action, report, export, event and log non-disclosure

sub_areas.title: Row policy precedes every read shape

evidence.proves: Row policy precedes direct, page, count, aggregate, include and relation reads.
Compiled row policy precedes paging on the real engine.
No allow rule compiles to an empty result.
Sensitive collections are filtered by exact resource scope.
Conditional field grants intersect and deny rules subtract.
A reference never releases a raw key without the target grant.
Validation errors do not reveal omitted fields.
Policy omission is not a field-existence oracle.
The disclosure view of a revision redacts secrets.
A secret field value appears in plaintext in no table, log record or read view.
An action is gated by its own row and action policy before mutation.
The portal cannot address an action the surface omits.
Action dispatch requires policy-filtered surface membership on every adapter.
Report, export and action plans inherit the operation policy.
A consolidated report returns exactly the member sites.
Consolidated reading is refused outside the group.
Every adapter reaches reports through the one policy-bound service.
An export publishes only under the policy it was requested with.
Export policy snapshots stay inside the export transaction.
A denied actor cannot queue a record export.
Browser downloads are CSRF protected and checksum verified.
Mutation events carry changed handles, never values.
Event checkpoints are isolated by site and organization.
A payload outside its signed schema never reaches a handler.
A forged context never enqueues an event.
The outbox, journal and audit rows a secret-bearing mutation writes carry no plaintext secret.
An MCP tool call writes none of its arguments to the log.
Every SDK payload shape is summarized before it reaches the logger.
Declared fields are redacted at every nesting level.
Payload objects are walked through their serialized form before formatting.
No request path or identifier reaches a metric label.
Studio media records only safe lifecycle metadata.

areas.title: Maker-checker, separation of duty, step-up, human proof and confused-deputy cases

evidence.proves: The requester cannot approve their own request.
One approver cannot vote twice, even from a second connection.
Racing approvers serialize on the request.
Consumption and revocation cannot both land.
Approver-only actors keep separation of duties on every surface.
A separation rule requires a live approval policy.
A changed rule invalidates pending requests.
The checker capability is frozen at request time.
Step-up codes are replay fenced and session bound.
Step-up is required on top of, never instead of, authority.
A step-up proof is consumed only under a live epoch.
MCP cannot perform an administrator step-up action.
The CLI cannot bypass administrator step-up.

sub_areas.title: Actions reserved to an accountable human

evidence.proves: No checker vote or secret input is reachable from an agent.
No MCP tool accepts a step-up credential.
Destructive purge planning is not reachable from an agent.
An agent cannot mint or rotate credentials.

sub_areas.title: Confused deputy across machine adapters and workers

evidence.proves: MCP keeps its caller provenance and refuses a foreign context.
The scheduler cannot borrow a foreign system principal.
The worker refuses a human context.
The CLI cannot select an organization the token does not carry.
REST refuses a client-selected organization.
The CLI refuses a submitted organization before authorization.
REST, MCP and CLI each accept only the credential minted for them.
A narrow credential cannot create through any of the three machine adapters.
No machine credential reaches a step-up-gated recovery act: REST and MCP publish none and the console is refused without a human step-up proof.
A machine credential cannot reach beyond its delegation ceiling by taking over a stronger account.
The delegation ceiling counts every grant path, direct and membership roles, before a credential changes hands.

sub_areas.title: Key reuse with different content and concurrent first claims

evidence.proves: A key reused with different content is refused.
A live reservation refuses a concurrent attempt.
The loser of a first claim never reaches the handler.
A replay refuses policy drift.
Over HTTP, the owner alone replays and reuse for other content is refused.

sub_areas.title: Keys are owned by actor, operation and resource

evidence.proves: A key presented under another credential is refused.
A key cannot probe or replay across resources.
An unauthorized request reserves nothing.
Revoked authority stops a keyed Studio replay.
The MCP idempotency binding is canonical.
Two actors sharing one key each run their own mutation; the key is scoped to its operation.
A revoked owner is refused before any replay.
The browser-parity REST mutations are authorized against their exact resource before the ledger is read.

areas.title: Extension signature, trust rotation, revocation and generation fencing

evidence.proves: Admission requires a valid signature from a trusted key.
Deployed bytes changed after verification are refused.
An edited package is refused at admission.
A tampered local publication is refused.
Rotation overlaps and refuses a final revoke under an active release.
Rotation cannot widen namespace constraints.
Final rotation refuses a disabled current release.
Over HTTP, an asset stays served through a rotation overlap and a premature final revocation is refused.
Emergency revocation quarantines the active release on every engine.
Revocation serializes with a concurrent install.
The signed revocation feed applies, refuses rollback and fails open loudly.
Revocation waits for an in-flight MCP transaction.
An emergency revocation withdraws the signed asset with the answer a missing file gets.
A stale trusted runtime drains before dispatch.
The generation fence is installed in the full runtime.
A stale generation refuses before any listener runs.
Jobs of an untrusted package never run.
A generation upgrade preserves active fences.
A process booted before any trust change is fenced with a retryable 503 over the live pipeline.

sub_areas.title: Ambient authority of admitted code and system principals

evidence.proves: The ambient-authority inventory ships with its deployment controls.
No surface claims admitted code is isolated.
Recovery composition reaches no extension code.
Custom handlers receive no transport, persistence or container.
An ordinary worker principal cannot run a privileged job.
A system context carries no scopes into extension code.
No server-wide advisory lock lets one installation hold ambient authority over another.

sub_areas.title: Out-of-process execution of untrusted extension code

out_of_scope.reason: Running untrusted extension code out of process is a runtime that does not exist yet; it belongs to the separate Point 5 extension track under GM-SUP-05. Until it lands, admitted PHP has full process authority and the product states so on every surface, which the posture evidence pins.

evidence.proves: Untrusted code is unsupported and the out-of-process route is named.

areas.title: Secret sources, rotation and redaction across every channel

evidence.proves: Secrets can come from protected files.
An ambiguous secret source is refused.
A weak application secret is refused.
Signing keys cannot reuse the application secret.
A configured origin cannot smuggle credentials into logs, audit and state.
Stored record secrets move onto the active key without loss.
An interrupted rotation resumes safely.
Rotating the application secret strands nothing.
A revoked key fails closed.
Previous keys are read from a protected key ring.

sub_areas.title: Redaction in log, problem, audit, replay, CLI and MCP channels

evidence.proves: Logged exceptions carry no trace or driver credential.
The wired logger writes no secret.
Credentials in messages, plain values and serializable objects are scrubbed.
Problem documents do not disclose exceptions.
A refused token is never echoed.
The metrics token is never echoed.
Audit metadata credentials are redacted before storage.
No writer records a credential-shaped audit key.
A token secret is never stored for replay.
The CLI accepts no raw secret option.
MCP payloads never reach the log.
A record secret is sealed in every table and absent from every log record.
A mutated row is detected.
A deletion inside an anchored range is detected.
Reordering is detected.
A tampered anchor ledger is detected.
The database refuses rewrites.
Tampering is detected without database enforcement.
The archive export is redacted, checksummed and audited.
Retention archives, anchors and prunes verifiably.
Reinserting a pruned row is detected.
Only the guarded retention window may delete.
The console export prints the manifest, never the bytes.

areas.title: Tenant isolation under concurrency and noisy-neighbour load

evidence.proves: A site-scoped actor cannot read or revoke another site token.
Revocation and issuance serialize on one fence.
Ownership removal cannot cross a site.
Membership scope cannot authorize a forged organization target.
A manager scoped to another site cannot read or rewrite the public site settings.
Settings management is authorized against the public site, never the caller site.
Concurrent writers in three sites never see each other menus and never lose their own.
A backlogged site cannot monopolise claim turns.
Fair tenant turns survive independent replicas.
Receipt fan-out keeps fair turns per site and organization.
Throttle budgets are keyed per subject and origin.
Two installations on one database server never contend for each other's lifecycle lock.
Every named advisory lock is scoped to its own database.
The preview grant is single use and frame hardened.
The preview channel is origin pinned and sequence checked.
Preview messages cannot be replayed.
An expired preview grant cannot be claimed.
The preview policy differs only in its frame directive.
The external fetch boundary carries every security stage.
Media mutations are audited transactionally.
Uploads are scoped and optimistically fenced.
No refusal discloses the candidate.
